title: Feature-driven capacity & labor sensitivity (working sheet)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet-style note to surface the near-term (Q1–Q3 2027) budget implications of three product-driven demand patterns: feature rollout (interactive chat), large enterprise onboarding (bursty heavy-embedding use), and normalization after quantization adoption. Goal is to map token/throughput scenarios to GPU-hours, marginal cost, and headcount phasing so finance and product can agree on trigger points for hiring and pricing changes.

TL;DR summary (high-level outputs):
- Baseline (current run-rate): 4.8B tokens/month, 26% gross margin on hosted API (after infra + ops).
- Feature surge (interactive chat feature rolled out to 2 pilot customers): tokens x2.8 -> projected margin drops to ~11% without pricing changes or capacity optimizations.
- Enterprise onboard (one 10% revenue customer with embedding-heavy queries): tokens x5 for that customer but concentrated; margin down to -3% if we reserve Dedicated GPUs for SLA.
- Quantization adoption (widespread 8-bit across eligible models): reduces per-token infra cost by ~28% improving margin by ~8–10 pts.

Quick assumptions (source inputs):
- Token to GPU-hour mapping: 1 GPU-hour ~= 200M tokens (median mix of decoder-only and encoder-decoder).
- Average GPU hourly cost (spot-blended): $2.90 (mix of spot/reserved for 2027 plan).
- Direct infra overhead (network, storage, licensing): 12% on top of GPU cost.
- Runway headcount hourly burden (ops + infra eng + SRE): loaded cost for hiring = $190k/year average -> ~$91/hr fully burdened.
- Burst reserve policy: reserve pool = 10% capacity of expected peak; burst pricing / premium passes cost 2.5x GPU-hour base.

Scenario table (rounded)
Scenario | tokens/mo | GPU-hours/mo | infra cost/mo | ops headcount add | margin (hosted)
Baseline | 4.8B | 24k | $84k | +0 FTE | 26%
Feature surge | 13.4B | 67k | $234k | +3 FTE (ops) | 11%
Enterprise onboard | 7.2B (org) + 4.8B base = 12B | 60k | $210k (+dedicated premiums) | +5 FTE (SRE+solutions) | -3%
Quantization applied | 4.8B | 24k | $61k (28% lower) | - | 34%

Notes on table: GPU-hours/mo derived by tokens / 200M. Infra cost = GPU-hours * blended GPU $2.9 + 12% overhead + any burst premium/Reserved uplift. Margin uses current revenue mix + per-route pricing (no price increase applied).

Headcount phasing (working plan):
- Current Q4 2026 baseline: Finance +2 headcount for billing ops scheduled (already hired). No additional hires budgeted.
- Trigger A (feature surge observed >2.5x sustained 6 weeks): hire 2 Customer Solutions engineers (on-call + runbooks) + 1 Capacity Ops (3 hires, ramp 6–10 weeks).
- Trigger B (customer concentration: 1 customer >8% revenue + tokens >15% monthly): hire 2 SRE + 1 Dedicated account manager (total 3 hires, ramp 8–12 weeks) AND evaluate reserved Dedicated pool purchase (commit vs burst).
- De-risk: accelerate quantization rollout in Optimize for top 20% of calls to avoid hires until 8-week mark.

Pricing sensitivity matrix (what to test):
1) Volume price step-downs for embeddings vs generation: incremental discount of 10%, 20%, 30% on volumes >X tokens/month; impact on take-rate and margin modeled.
2) SLA surcharge for enterprise: +12–20% surcharge for guaranteed p50/p95 latency with Dedicated; how much reduces churn?
3) Tiered burst fees: immediate 2.5x GPU-hour price for ad-hoc bursts vs prepaid burst credits at 1.6x.

Sensitivity run (selected outputs):
- If we implement SLA surcharge +15% for enterprise onboarding and keep baseline volume pricing: Enterprise scenario margin moves from -3% to +6% (but may reduce sign-up probability by ~25%, product to validate).
- If we add a 15% embedding volume discount above 2T tokens/mo, feature surge margin drops another 2–3 pts. Net effect depends on customer elasticity.
- Rolling quantization on top-20% routes recovers ~4 pts of margin in feature surge scenario (operational complexity assumed +0.4 FTE for rollout support).

Risks and concentration notes:
- Single-customer embedding heavy load introduces runaway token velocity and operational spike. Recommendation: gating token velocity in the onboarding contract or requiring Dedicated commitment for sustained >X tokens/day.
- Hiring lag (8–12 weeks) means margin deterioration can persist unless pricing or optimizations are applied early.
- Spot GPU price shocks: +30% spot price increases can flip the feature surge scenario from 11% margin to ~-2%. Need spot hedge/reserve policy.

Open questions (to resolve in next sync):
- Product: what is the expected conversion rate of the pilot chat feature to broader customers? paper-estimate numbers? (Action: Derek to provide p50/p90 adoption curve by 2026-12-10).
- Sales: willingness to accept SLA surcharge vs sell Dedicated seats — data from last two enterprise renewals (Action: Sofia to pull contract terms by 2026-12-08).
- Eng/Runtime: feasibility and timeline to template quantization rollout for top models (Action: Noah to give ETA and risk matrix by 2026-12-12).

Decision options for finance (quick):
- Option 1: Hold hiring until signs hit triggers A/B; implement temporary emergency burst surcharge (2.5x) immediately for new large customers.
- Option 2: Pre-commit to a small Dedicated pool now (3 GPUs reserved equivalently), budgeted and capitalized, to protect margins for enterprise sign-ups.
- Option 3: Accelerate Optimize incentives (credits to customers to switch to quantized variants) and allocate 0.5 FTE to support migration to avoid hires.

Next steps and owners:
- Derek Liu: produce adoption curve scenarios for chat pilot (due 2026-12-10).
- Sofia Alvarez: extract recent enterprise contract terms and pricing elasticity notes (due 2026-12-08).
- Noah Patel: quantization rollout ETA + risk list (due 2026-12-12).
- Maya Chen (owner): consolidate a hiring trigger memo and propose a 3-month runway contingency (due 2026-12-14).

Appendix (mini-calcs):
- tokens->GPU-hours calc example: 13.4B tokens / 200M = 67 GPU-hours (x1000 = 67k GPU-hours/mo).
- Infra cost feature surge (simple): 67k GPU-hrs * $2.9 = $194.3k; +12% overhead -> $217.2k; + burst reserve premium (if 10% of those hours at 2.5x) add ~$16k -> ~233k.

Notes-to-self: document is a working artifact. Keep conservative rounding. If team wants, I can export a small sheet with scenario sliders (tokens multiplier, quantization %, surcharge %) and automated outputs.
